question: 语言塑造思维吗？说不同语言的人，看到的是不同的世界吗？
question_en: Does language shape thought? Do speakers of different languages see different worlds?

casting.reason: 她把这道题拽进实验室：母语会不会悄悄改变你对颜色、时间、因果的知觉与记忆？她的答案是温和的『会』——不是锁死，而是给注意力上偏置，且效应可测、有大有小。
casting.reason_en: She drags this question into the lab: does your mother tongue quietly alter how you perceive and remember color, time and causation? Her answer is a moderate 'yes' — not a lock but a bias on attention, measurable and varying in size.

casting.reason: 他站在相反一端：语言是人类天生、物种共享的官能，各语言深层同构，那点表层差异触不到思维的引擎。他更提醒，把语言说成牢笼，恰恰方便有人用词语替你划定能想什么。
casting.reason_en: He stands at the opposite pole: language is an innate, species-shared faculty, its depths the same across tongues, and surface differences never reach the engine of thought. He warns, too, that calling language a prison is just what lets others use words to fence off what you may think.

casting.reason: 他从治世看语言：名不正则言不顺、事不成。命名与名分不是记事的工具，而是社会秩序的纲纪——名一乱，是非淆、人心散，故必先正名。
casting.reason_en: He views language through governance: if names are not rectified, speech and affairs fail. Naming and role are no mere recording device but the cord of social order — let names blur and right and wrong scatter, so names must first be set right.

casting.reason: 他反其道：道可道非常道，名可名非常名。命名即切割，把浑全之朴劈成彼此好恶；真知无待于言，得意则忘言。名愈正，他说，去道愈远。
casting.reason_en: He runs the other way: the Way that can be spoken is not the constant Way. To name is to cut, splitting the uncarved whole into this-and-that, liking and loathing; true knowing needs no words. The straighter the names, he says, the farther from the Way.

casting.reason: 他把语言看穿为一支『流动的隐喻大军』：所谓真理只是磨光了的比喻，主谓语法哄我们相信有个『我』在『思考』。只要还信语法，就还没摆脱上帝。
casting.reason_en: He sees through language as a 'mobile army of metaphors': what we call truth is only worn-smooth figures, and subject-predicate grammar coaxes us to believe in an 'I' that 'thinks.' So long as we believe in grammar, he says, we are not rid of God.

casting.reason: 他把语言抬到存在的高度：语言不是人手中的工具，而是存在之家——语言先向我们开显世界，人方能栖居其中。故是语言说话，人只应和。
casting.reason_en: He raises language to the level of Being: language is not a tool in human hands but the house of Being — it first opens a world to us, in which we may dwell. So language speaks, and the human only answers.

casting.reason: 他要把话拉回地面：语言常因坏语法误导人，但出路是逻辑分析而非投降。说清同一事实的不同语言，表达的是同一个命题；工具会出毛病，但工具可以磨。
casting.reason_en: He brings it back to earth: language misleads through bad grammar, but the cure is logical analysis, not surrender. Different languages that state the same fact clearly express one and the same proposition; a tool malfunctions, but a tool can be honed.

casting.reason: 他从最底层的人看语言：旧文言把四万万人挡在思想门外，所以要用白话让人开得了口。改造语言是为改造被旧字句捆住的国民性——能说话的人，才谈得上有思想。
casting.reason_en: He sees language from the very bottom: Classical Chinese shut four hundred million out of thought, so the vernacular was needed to let them speak. To reform language was to reform a national character bound by old phrases — only those who can speak can be said to have thoughts.

casting.reason: 他从人类学取最宽的视角：表层的语言与神话千差万别，底层却共用同一副心智骨架——同样的二元对立、同样的调解。差异真实，但差异之下，人同此心。
casting.reason_en: He takes the widest, anthropological view: languages and myths differ wildly on the surface, yet share one skeleton of mind beneath — the same binary oppositions, the same mediations. Difference is real, but beneath it the human heart is one.

posts.text: 别把这题当哲学空谈——它能进实验室。俄语把浅蓝(goluboy)和深蓝(siniy)当两个基本颜色词，结果俄语者区分这两种蓝的反应就是更快；澳洲 Kuuk Thaayorre 人没有『左右』，只说东南西北，于是他们永远知道自己朝哪、连时间都按太阳排布。**语言不是给思想穿的衣服，它是给注意力装的一副眼镜——你被反复要求留意什么，久了就真的更容易看见什么。**我不说它锁死你的思想，我说它悄悄给你的认知上了偏置。
posts.text_en: Don't treat this as armchair philosophy — it goes into the lab. Russian makes light blue (goluboy) and dark blue (siniy) two basic color words, and Russian speakers are measurably faster at telling those two blues apart; the Kuuk Thaayorre of Australia have no 'left' or 'right,' only north-south-east-west, so they always know which way they face, and even lay out time by the sun. **Language is not clothing you drape over thought; it is a pair of glasses fitted onto attention — what you are made to notice again and again, in time you really do see more readily.** I don't claim it locks your thinking; I claim it quietly puts a bias on your cognition.

glossary.Kuuk Thaayorre: Kuuk Thaayorre（库克·塔约雷语）：澳洲约克角一支原住民语言，不用『左/右』这类以身体为中心的方位，只用绝对的东南西北，说话者因此需时刻知道自己的朝向。
glossary.偏置: bias（偏置）：不至于决定结论、却让某个方向更省力、更易被想到的系统性倾斜；此处指母语让某些区分、某些注意更容易发生。

glossary_en.Kuuk Thaayorre: An Aboriginal language of Cape York, Australia that uses no body-centered 'left/right' but only absolute compass directions, so its speakers must always track their orientation.
glossary_en.bias: A systematic tilt that does not fix the conclusion but makes one direction easier, more available; here, the way a mother tongue makes certain distinctions and forms of attention come more readily.

posts.text: 我恰好从相反方向看。全世界几千种语言，表面千差万别，深处却共享一套普遍语法——每个正常孩子在证据少得可怜的情况下，几年内就长出母语，靠的是天生的语言官能。颜色词、方位词那点差异是真的，但它撬动的是边缘的知觉习惯，不是思维的引擎。人类先有概念、有心智运算，才拿语言把它外化。真正该警惕的，恰恰是反过来：**把语言当成牢笼，正好方便有人用词语替你圈定『什么可想、什么不可说』。**
posts.text_en: I see it from the opposite side. The world's thousands of languages differ wildly on the surface, yet deep down share a Universal Grammar — every normal child, on absurdly thin evidence, grows a mother tongue in a few years, drawing on an innate language faculty. The differences in color words and direction terms are real, but what they move is a fringe of perceptual habit, not the engine of thought. Humans have concepts and mental computation first, and only then use language to externalize them. What truly deserves suspicion is the reverse: **treat language as a prison, and you make it easy for someone to use words to fence off for you what may be thought and what may not be said.**

glossary.普遍语法: Universal Grammar（普遍语法）：乔姆斯基提出的假说，认为人类各种语言底下共享一套先天的语法原则，孩子据此能在有限输入下迅速习得母语。
glossary.语言官能: the language faculty（语言官能）：人脑中专司语言的先天认知系统，使语言习得成为人类物种普遍、可靠的能力，而非纯靠环境灌输。

glossary_en.Universal Grammar: Chomsky's hypothesis that beneath the world's diverse languages lies a shared set of innate grammatical principles, by which a child can rapidly acquire a mother tongue from limited input.
glossary_en.language faculty: The innate, language-specific cognitive system in the human brain that makes language acquisition a universal, reliable trait of the species rather than mere environmental conditioning.

posts.text: 为政必也正名乎！名不正，则言不顺；言不顺，则事不成；事不成，则礼乐不兴，刑罚不中，民无所措手足。故君子于其言，无所苟而已矣。**名者，治之始也：名一乱，则是非淆、人心散。**语言非徒记事之器，乃立世之纲。名定而后分明，分明而后天下可安。
posts.text_en: In governing, surely one must first attend to the rectification of names. If names are not rectified, speech does not accord; if speech does not accord, affairs are not completed; if affairs fail, rites and music do not flourish, punishments miss their mark, and the people have nowhere to put hand or foot. So the noble person is never careless in a single word. **Names are where governance begins: let names fall into confusion, and right and wrong blur, and the people's hearts scatter.** Language is no mere device for recording things; it is the very cord that holds a life and a state upright. Only when names are fixed are distinctions clear, and only with clear distinctions can the world be at peace.
posts.vernacular: 要治理天下，一定得先端正名分！名分不端正，说话就不顺当；说话不顺，事情就办不成；事情办不成，礼乐兴不起来，刑罚也落不到点子上，百姓就手足无措、不知怎么办才好。所以君子用词，从不敢马虎。**名分是治理的起点：名一乱，是非就跟着混、人心就跟着散。**语言不只是记事的工具，而是安身立世的纲纪。名定了才有分际，有分际了天下才能安定。

glossary.正名: rectification of names（正名）：孔子的主张，要求让名称、名分与其所指的实际、责任相符——君臣父子各如其名，语言一旦名实相符，社会秩序才能成立。

glossary_en.rectification of names: Confucius's doctrine that names, titles and roles must be made to match the realities and duties they denote — ruler, minister, father, son each living up to the name — so that once language fits fact, social order can stand.

posts.text: 道可道，非常道；名可名，非常名。天下万物生于有，有生于无。名者，割也——一名立，则彼此判、好恶起，浑全之朴自此裂。**上士闻道，不以言为极，而以言为筌；得鱼则忘筌，得意则忘言。**孔丘欲正名以治世，吾则见名愈正、去道愈远。为学日益，为道日损。真知无待于言，塞其兑、闭其门，而天下之理自明。
posts.text_en: The Way that can be spoken is not the constant Way; the name that can be named is not the constant name. The ten thousand things are born of Being, and Being is born of Nothing. To name is to cut — set up one name and 'this' and 'that,' liking and loathing part, and the uncarved block (pu) is split. **The finest hearer of the Way takes words not as the end but as a fish-trap; get the fish and you forget the trap, grasp the meaning and you forget the words.** Kong Qiu would rectify names to govern the world; I see that the straighter the names, the farther from the Way. In learning you add day by day; in the Way you subtract day by day. True knowing needs no words — block the mouth, shut the gate, and the pattern of the world grows clear of itself.
posts.vernacular: 可以言说的道，就不是恒常的道；可以命名的名，就不是恒常的名。天下万物生于『有』，而『有』生于『无』。命名，其实是一种切割——一个名字立起来，你我、好坏就跟着分开，本来浑然一体的朴素就此破裂。**上等的人听闻大道，不把语言当终点，只当捕鱼的竹篓；捞到鱼就忘掉篓，领会了意思就忘掉言辞。**孔丘想靠正名来治理天下，我却看到：名分越是端正，离道反而越远。求学问一天天做加法，求道却要一天天做减法。真正的了悟不依赖语言——堵住嘴、关上门，天下的道理自会明白。

glossary.朴: the uncarved block（朴）：老子用来喻指未被名称、分别切割过的原初浑全之境；一旦命名、区分，这份完整就被『雕琢』破坏。

glossary_en.the uncarved block: Laozi's image (Chinese pu) for the original, undivided wholeness before names and distinctions carve it up; to name is to split that intactness.

posts.text: 你们争语言塑不塑造思维，太天真——语言从一开始就是一支**流动的隐喻大军**，是我们把神经刺激先译成图像、再译成声音，然后忘了这是翻译，把它当成了『真理』。『主语—谓语』的语法哄着你相信：有个『我』在『思考』，有个东西在『存在』。我说：**只要我们还相信语法，就还没能摆脱上帝。**概念是把无数不相等的东西抹平成『相等』的骗术。所以别问语言忠不忠实于世界——它压根不是为真理造的，是为活下去、为支配造的。
posts.text_en: You argue whether language shapes thought — too naive. Language was from the start **a mobile army of metaphors**: we translate a nerve-stimulus first into an image, then into a sound, and then forget it was translation and call it 'truth.' The subject-predicate grammar coaxes you into believing there is an 'I' that 'thinks,' a thing that 'is.' I say: **so long as we still believe in grammar, we have not yet got rid of God.** A concept is the swindle of smoothing countless unequal things into 'the equal.' So do not ask whether language is faithful to the world — it was never built for truth, but for surviving, for mastery.

glossary.流动的隐喻大军: a mobile army of metaphors（流动的隐喻大军）：尼采的说法，指所谓真理其实是一堆隐喻、转喻用久了、磨光了感性棱角后，被当成客观事实的东西；语言并非映照世界，而是层层比喻的沉积。

glossary_en.a mobile army of metaphors: Nietzsche's phrase: what we call truth is really a heap of metaphors and metonymies that, worn smooth by long use, get taken for objective fact; language does not mirror the world but is a sediment of figures.

posts.text: 诸位都把语言当成一件工具——人先在，然后拿起语言来用。这正是最深的误解。不是我们支配语言，而是语言先向我们开显了一个世界，我们才得以在其中『存在』。**语言是存在之家；人居住在语言所筑的屋里。**一个没有『远方』『思念』这些词的民族，不是缺了工具，而是缺了一整片可栖居的天地。故而语言说话，人只是应和它而说。诗与思守护语言，正因语言守护着我们与存在的照面。
posts.text_en: You all take language for a tool — the human is first, and then picks language up to use. That is the deepest error. It is not that we command language; rather language first opens a world to us, so that we may 'be' within it. **Language is the house of Being; the human dwells in the house that language builds.** A people without words like 'the far distance' or 'longing' lacks not a tool but a whole habitable region. So language speaks, and the human only answers after it. Poetry and thinking keep watch over language precisely because language keeps watch over our encounter with Being.

glossary.存在之家: the house of Being（存在之家）：海德格尔的名喻，指语言不是人手中的器具，而是存在向人显现、人得以领会万物『是其所是』的场所；人栖居于语言，才与世界照面。

glossary_en.the house of Being: Heidegger's image: language is not an instrument in human hands but the dwelling in which Being shows itself and the human comes to understand things as what they are; we dwell in language, and only so meet the world.

posts.text: 让我把话拉回地面。语言当然会误导人——正因为日常语法的表层，藏着逻辑的真形。『金山不存在』这句，语法上像在说某座山、其实一分析就明白（此即摹状词分析），它只否定『有 x 既是金的又是山』。**大量所谓深奥的哲学难题，不过是被坏语法绊倒的常识；把命题拆到逻辑骨架上，谜团自会散去。**说不同语言的人若都讲清同一件事实，他们表达的是同一个命题。语言是件常出毛病的工具——但工具可以磨。磨好它，我们看见的是同一个世界，不是各自的幻境。
posts.text_en: Let me bring this back to earth. Language does mislead — precisely because beneath the surface of everyday grammar hides the true logical form. 'The golden mountain does not exist' looks grammatically like a remark about some mountain, yet on analysis (this is the theory of descriptions) it merely denies that 'there is an x that is both golden and a mountain.' **A great many so-called deep philosophical puzzles are just common sense tripped by bad grammar; take a proposition down to its logical skeleton and the fog lifts.** If speakers of different languages each state the same fact clearly, they express one and the same proposition. Language is a tool that often malfunctions — but a tool can be honed. Hone it, and what we see is one world, not each our own phantasm.

glossary.命题: proposition（命题）：一句话所断定的、可为真为假的那个内容本身，独立于用哪种语言、哪串词句来表达；罗素认为不同语言若讲清同一事实，表达的是同一个命题。
glossary.摹状词: theory of descriptions（摹状词）：罗素的分析方法，把『那个金山』这类看似指称某物的短语，改写成一串存在与唯一性的断言，从而消解『不存在之物为何能被谈论』这类假难题。

glossary_en.proposition: The content a sentence asserts — what can be true or false — independent of which language or string of words expresses it; Russell holds that if different languages state the same fact clearly, they express the same proposition.
glossary_en.theory of descriptions: Russell's method of rewriting phrases like 'the golden mountain,' which seem to name a thing, as a string of existence-and-uniqueness claims, dissolving pseudo-problems such as how a non-existent thing can be spoken of.

posts.text: 你们在云端谈道谈逻辑，我却看见地上的人。旧中国把文言锁在少数人手里，方块字艰深，四万万人多半不识字、不能读、不能想自己的处境——**语言在这里不是中性的工具，它是一道墙，把绝大多数人挡在思想的门外。**所以我们才拼命推白话文：让人能用自己嘴里的话去写、去读、去愤怒。改造语言，是为了改造那被旧字句捆住的国民性。名相不必先正，先让老百姓开得了口。能说话的人，才谈得上有思想。
posts.text_en: You speak of the Way and of logic up in the clouds; I see the people on the ground. Old China locked classical Chinese in the hands of a few; the square characters were forbidding, and four hundred million people, mostly unlettered, could not read, could not think through their own plight — **here language is no neutral tool but a wall, shutting the vast majority outside the gate of thought.** That is why we fought so hard for vernacular Chinese: so that people could write, read and rage in the very words of their own mouths. To reform the language was to reform a national character bound up by the old phrases. Names need not be rectified first; first let the common people be able to open their mouths. Only those who can speak can be said to have thoughts.

glossary.白话文: vernacular Chinese（白话文）：以口语为基础的现代书面汉语，二十世纪初新文化运动用它取代艰深的文言，让普通人能读能写，鲁迅是主将之一。
glossary.国民性: national character（国民性）：鲁迅常用的说法，指一个民族在长期历史、语言与制度中养成的普遍心理与行为习性；他认为语言文字的改造是改造这种习性的关键一环。

glossary_en.vernacular Chinese: Modern written Chinese based on everyday speech (baihua); the early-20th-century New Culture Movement used it to replace forbidding Classical Chinese so ordinary people could read and write, with Lu Xun a leading champion.
glossary_en.national character: Lu Xun's recurring term for the shared psychology and habits a people forms through long history, language and institutions; he saw reform of the written language as central to reforming those habits.

posts.text: 我在亚马逊丛林里住过，得出的结论和猎奇式的想象相反：所谓『原始人』的思维，和你我一样精密。他们对上千种动植物的分类之细，堪比植物学家——**人类的心灵到处都在用同一套办法运转：把世界劈成一对对二元对立（生/熟、自然/文化），再在其间调解。**表面上语言五花八门，深层结构却是同一部人类精神的语法。所以我既不信语言把各族锁进不同世界，也不信它只是透明工具——它是文化借以显影的介质，而底片，是共通的。
posts.text_en: I lived in the Amazon forest, and reached a conclusion opposite to the exotic-tourist view: the thought of so-called 'primitives' is as precise as yours or mine. Their classification of a thousand plants and animals rivals a botanist's — **the human mind everywhere runs on the same procedure: it splits the world into binary oppositions (raw/cooked, nature/culture) and then mediates between them.** On the surface languages are wildly various; in the depths the structure is one grammar of the human spirit. So I believe neither that language locks each people into a different world, nor that it is a transparent tool — it is the medium through which culture develops like a photograph, and the negative is shared.

glossary.二元对立: binary opposition（二元对立）：列维-斯特劳斯结构主义的核心分析单位，认为人类心灵普遍倾向把经验组织成成对的对立范畴（生/熟、自然/文化），神话与亲属制度都是在这些对立间反复调解的产物。

glossary_en.binary opposition: The core analytic unit of Lévi-Strauss's structuralism: the human mind everywhere tends to organize experience into paired opposites (raw/cooked, nature/culture), and myth and kinship are endless mediations between such pairs.

posts.text: 波洛迪茨基的实验我尊重，但请看清它的量级。俄语者辨蓝快了几十毫秒，一戴上颜色干扰任务、一让他们心里默数，这点优势就蒸发了——**它活在知觉的边角，碰不到你推理、算数、构句的核心。**更别提方法学：这类效应屡屡被重复失败。真正惊人的不是差异，而是普遍性：一个中国孩子和一个巴西孩子，长出的语法结构深处如出一辙。你把偏置说得温柔，可一旦它被政治语言利用，那副『眼镜』就成了别人给你戴的。
posts.text_en: I respect Boroditsky's experiments, but see their magnitude. Russian speakers are faster at blues by tens of milliseconds — load them with a color-interference task, or have them count silently, and that edge evaporates. **It lives at the margins of perception; it never touches the core where you reason, calculate, build a sentence.** And the methodology: such effects fail to replicate again and again. What is truly astonishing is not the difference but the universality — a Chinese child and a Brazilian child grow the same deep grammatical structure. You make 'bias' sound gentle, but once political language exploits it, those 'glasses' are put on you by someone else.

posts.text: 『碰不到核心』？我们测的正是核心。让英语者和讲 Kuuk Thaayorre 的人给时间排序，英语者从左到右、希伯来语者从右到左、原住民却按东西方向排——这是在推理里，不是在辨色边角里。西班牙语者更容易记住『打碎花瓶的是谁』的替代说法：他们的语言爱说『花瓶自己碎了』，于是连记忆里的『谁之过』都淡了。复制失败有，稳健重复的也一大把。我从不说语法锁死思想；我说**它在你没察觉时，替你把默认选项调好了。**这恰恰更该警惕，不是更不必。
posts.text_en: 'Never touches the core'? The core is exactly what we test. Ask English and Kuuk Thaayorre speakers to arrange time: the English go left-to-right, Hebrew speakers right-to-left, and the Aboriginal group lay it out by east and west — that is inside reasoning, not at the fringe of color. Spanish speakers more readily remember the agentless version of who broke a vase: their language likes 'the vase broke itself,' and so even the memory of 'whose fault' fades. Yes, some studies fail to replicate; plenty also replicate robustly. I never say grammar locks thought; I say **while you're not looking, it sets your defaults for you.** That deserves more suspicion, not less.

glossary.默认选项: default（默认选项）：在你不特意选择时系统自动采用的那一项；波洛迪茨基借它比喻母语替你预设好的注意与记忆方式——不排斥别的选择，却让某一种最省力、最先浮现。

glossary_en.default: The option a system adopts automatically when you make no deliberate choice; Boroditsky's metaphor for the ways of attending and remembering a mother tongue pre-sets for you — not barring other choices, but making one the easiest, the first to surface.

posts.text: 尼采说真理不过是隐喻大军——可这句话本身，是要我们当真、当真的。**若一切断言都只是比喻、无所谓真假，那『一切都是隐喻』这句也就自我拆台了。**我承认语法会把常识引进沟里，但出路是分析，不是投降。『我思故我在』里那个可疑的『我』，正该用逻辑解剖、而非用更多华丽的隐喻去顶替。你把语言的病诊断得极准，开的药却是继续发烧。我要的是退烧：把话说清楚，让分歧显出到底是关于事实，还是只关于用词。
posts.text_en: Nietzsche says truth is only an army of metaphors — yet that very sentence asks us to take it as true. **If every assertion is mere metaphor, neither true nor false, then 'all is metaphor' saws off its own branch.** I grant that grammar leads common sense into the ditch, but the way out is analysis, not surrender. The dubious 'I' in 'I think therefore I am' should be dissected by logic, not replaced by yet more gorgeous metaphors. You diagnose the sickness of language exactly, then prescribe more fever. I want the fever down: say it clearly, and let a dispute show whether it is about facts or only about words.

posts.text: 罗素，你的『逻辑真形』是什么？无非是又一套语法，被你供上了神坛。你把命题拆成符号，以为触到了世界的骨架——**可那套逻辑的骨架，本身就是印欧语『主语＋谓语＋系词是』长出来的偏见。**换一种语言，连『存在』这个动词都未必有，你的『金山不存在』又从何谈起？你想退烧，我却说：发烧才是清醒——承认没有中性的语言、没有语言之外的裸事实，才是诚实。你磨你的工具，磨到最后，照见的还是磨刀人自己的手。
posts.text_en: Russell, what is your 'true logical form'? Only another grammar, which you have set on an altar. You break a proposition into symbols and fancy you have touched the world's skeleton — **but that logical skeleton is itself a prejudice grown from the Indo-European subject-predicate-copula.** In another language there may be no verb 'to be' at all, so where does your 'the golden mountain does not exist' even begin? You want the fever down; I say the fever is the lucidity — to admit there is no neutral language, no bare fact outside language, is the honest thing. Hone your tool, and at the end what it reflects is the honer's own hand.

glossary.系词: copula（系词）：把主语和表语连起来、相当于『是』的成分（英语的 be）；尼采与不少语言学家指出，许多语言并无独立的系词，故以『是/存在』为根的西方形而上学未必普适。

glossary_en.copula: The element linking subject and predicate, the 'is' (English be); Nietzsche and many linguists note that many languages lack a separate copula, so a Western metaphysics rooted in 'is/being' may not be universal.

posts.text: 仲尼欲正名而安天下，吾恐名愈正而伪愈滋。**大道废，有仁义；智慧出，有大伪——名相一立，争端随之。**民之难治，以其智多；令繁名密，则民弥巧于避。太上，下知有之；不尚贤，不贵难得之货，使民心不乱。故治国不在正其名，而在复其朴。绝圣弃智，民利百倍；绝仁弃义，民复孝慈。名者末也，无名之朴，方为治本。
posts.text_en: Kong Qiu would rectify names to settle the world; I fear the straighter the names, the more falsehood breeds. **When the great Way declines, 'benevolence and righteousness' appear; when cleverness arises, great hypocrisy follows — set up a name and strife comes with it.** The people are hard to govern because they scheme too much; the denser the decrees and titles, the craftier they grow at dodging them. The best ruler is one the people barely know is there; exalt no worthies, prize no rare goods, and their hearts stay unstirred. So governing lies not in rectifying names but in returning to the uncarved block. Drop sagehood and cleverness, and the people gain a hundredfold; drop preachy benevolence, and they return of themselves to filial love. Names are the twig; the nameless uncarved simplicity is the root of order.
posts.vernacular: 孔丘想靠端正名分来安定天下，我却担心：名分越端正，虚伪反而越滋生。**大道废弃了，才有人标举『仁义』；智巧出现了，才有大伪诈——名目一立，争端就跟着来。**百姓难治理，正因为心机太多；政令一繁、名目一密，百姓就越会钻空子躲避。最好的治理，是百姓只隐约知道有个君主而已；不标榜贤能、不看重稀罕之物，民心自然不乱。所以治国不在于端正名分，而在于回到那份未经雕琢的朴素。抛开所谓圣智，百姓得利百倍；抛开硬性的仁义说教，百姓反倒重新孝顺慈爱。名分是末节，无名的朴，才是治理的根本。

glossary.无名之朴: the nameless uncarved simplicity（无名之朴）：老子理想的治理与存在状态，先于一切名目、分别、标榜；他认为回到这份未命名的浑全，胜过用端正名分去管理。

glossary_en.the nameless uncarved simplicity: Laozi's ideal state of rule and being, prior to all names, distinctions and moral display; he holds that returning to this unnamed wholeness surpasses governing by rectified names.

posts.text: 老聃归朴而弃名，其言美矣，然坐言者谁之力？**无名则父子无别、君臣无分，孝慈忠信皆无处系——名亡而后乱作。**婴孩之爱亦须『父』『母』之名以立人伦之别。汝安处山林、忘言得意，正赖众人各守其名、耕者有其名、守者有其名，方成汝忘言之地。故正名非缚民，乃所以护民。名正则言顺，言顺则民有所依；去名求朴，朴未得而乱先至矣。
posts.text_en: Lao Dan would return to simplicity and cast off names; the words are lovely — but by whose labor do you sit and speak them? **Without names, father and son are undivided, ruler and minister undistinguished, and filial love, loyalty and good faith have nowhere to rest — let names perish and disorder breaks out.** Even an infant's love needs the names 'father' and 'mother' to stand up as the human bonds. You dwell at ease in the hills, forgetting words to grasp the meaning, precisely because everyone else keeps to his name — the farmer to the farmer's, the guard to the guard's — and so make you the very ground on which you may forget words. So rectifying names does not bind the people; it shields them. Names rectified, speech accords; speech according, the people have something to lean on. Strip names to chase simplicity, and before simplicity is won, disorder has already come.
posts.vernacular: 老聃主张回到朴素、抛开名分，话是说得漂亮，可你能安坐着谈玄，是靠谁撑着的呢？**没有名分，父子就没了分别、君臣就没了分际，孝慈忠信统统无处安放——名一旦亡失，祸乱随之而起。**连婴孩对亲人的爱，也要靠『父』『母』这样的名分才立得起人伦。你安居山林、忘掉言辞去体会意趣，恰恰是仰仗众人各守其名——种田的守着种田的名分、看守的守着看守的名分，才成全了你那片可以忘言的天地。所以端正名分不是捆绑百姓，而是保护百姓。名分正了说话才顺，说话顺了百姓才有依靠；一味去掉名分去求朴素，朴素没求到，祸乱倒先来了。

glossary.人伦: the human bonds（人伦）：儒家指父子、君臣、夫妇、长幼、朋友等基本人际关系及其应有之义；孔子认为这些关系要靠正名——各安其名分——才立得起来。

glossary_en.the human bonds: In Confucianism, the basic relations — father-son, ruler-minister, husband-wife, elder-younger, friend-friend — and their proper duties; Confucius holds these stand only through the rectification of names, each keeping to his role.

posts.text: 『得意忘言』『塞其兑闭其门』——听着高妙，可这四个字，两千年里成了聪明人偷懒、糊涂人认命的护身符。**当大多数人连话都说不利索时，劝他们『忘言』，无异于劝饿肚子的人少吃。**忘言是吃饱了的人的奢侈。老先生要回到无名之朴，我却要给还没有名字的痛苦一个名字：叫它『吃人』，叫它『瞒和骗』。语言最要紧的用处，不是通向那个玄妙的道，而是让被踩在最底下的人，第一次能指着自己的处境说：这不对。
posts.text_en: 'Forget words once you grasp the meaning,' 'block the mouth, shut the gate' — it sounds sublime, but for two thousand years these phrases have been an amulet for the clever to shirk and the muddled to resign. **When most people can barely get a sentence out, to urge them to 'forget words' is to tell the starving to eat less.** Forgetting words is the luxury of the well-fed. The old master would return to the nameless simplicity; I would give a name to suffering that has none — call it 'devouring people,' call it 'the lie and the cheat.' The most vital use of language is not the road to some mysterious Way, but to let those trodden at the very bottom point at their own condition and say, for the first time: this is wrong.

glossary.吃人: 'devouring people'（吃人）：鲁迅《狂人日记》中的意象，指旧礼教在温情名义下对个体的吞噬；他借为无名的压迫命名，让人得以指认并反抗它。

glossary_en.devouring people: An image from Lu Xun's 'A Madman's Diary': the old ethical order, under a veneer of warmth, consuming the individual; by naming a nameless oppression he lets people recognize and resist it.

posts.text: 乔姆斯基把语言官能装进大脑，当作一套可计算的先天机制——这是把语言彻底技术化，也是我们时代最深的迷误。**你能穷尽语法的规则，却算不出一句诗为何让人在词语里忽然照见存在。**普遍语法或许解释了人怎样造句，却答不了：为什么正是在语言中，世界才作为世界向我们敞开？把语言降为信息处理，人就从『语言的居住者』沦为『语言的操作员』。技术能造出会说话的机器，却造不出一种栖居。
posts.text_en: Chomsky fits the language faculty into the brain as a computable innate mechanism — this is to make language wholly technical, the deepest delusion of our age. **You may exhaust the rules of grammar and still never compute why a line of poetry lets a person suddenly glimpse Being within the words.** Universal Grammar may explain how one builds a sentence, but it cannot answer: why is it precisely in language that the world opens to us as world? Reduce language to information processing, and the human sinks from 'inhabitant of language' to 'operator of language.' Technology can build a machine that talks, but not a dwelling.

glossary.栖居: dwelling（栖居）：海德格尔用语，指人本真地安居于世、与存在照面的方式；他认为人本应作为『语言的居住者』栖居于语言，而技术化的语言观把人贬为语言的操作员。

glossary_en.dwelling: Heidegger's term for the human's authentic being-at-home in the world and encounter with Being; he holds we should dwell in language as its 'inhabitants,' whereas a technological view of language reduces us to its operators.

posts.text: 尼采说语言是一支无政府的隐喻大军，各自为战、无真理可言——可我在神话里看到的恰恰相反。从亚马逊到古希腊，成千上万个彼此不通的神话，翻来覆去用同几组神话素、讲同几组对立：生与熟、天与地、生与死。**表层的隐喻千变万化，底层的句法却惊人地守恒——那不是混沌，那是人类精神共用的一副骨架。**所以语言既没把各族关进不同宇宙（他们的深层逻辑相通），也不是尼采式的任意漂流。差异真实，但差异之下，人同此心。
posts.text_en: Nietzsche calls language an anarchic army of metaphors, each at war, with no truth to be had — yet in myth I find the very opposite. From the Amazon to ancient Greece, thousands of mutually unintelligible myths tell, over and over, with the same mythemes, the same handful of oppositions: raw and cooked, sky and earth, life and death. **The surface metaphors shift endlessly, but the underlying syntax is astonishingly conserved — that is not chaos, it is a skeleton shared by the human spirit.** So language neither shuts each people in a separate cosmos (their deep logic is common) nor drifts arbitrarily as Nietzsche would have it. Difference is real, but beneath difference, the human heart is one.

glossary.神话素: mytheme（神话素）：列维-斯特劳斯借语言学的音位概念提出的分析单位，指神话中可重复组合的最小意义单元；他发现不同文化的神话由相似的神话素、按相似的对立法则拼合。

glossary_en.mytheme: The minimal unit of meaning in myth, coined by Lévi-Strauss on the model of the phoneme; he found that myths of different cultures are assembled from similar mythemes by similar rules of opposition.

posts.text: 把三轮吵完的东西收一收：语言不给你思想的锁链，但它天天在你耳边**调低某些念头的门槛、调高另一些**。这不是玄学，是可测量的偏置。给普通人的用法有三条：一，学一门外语——哪怕只学到能吵架，你会突然发现有些情绪你母语里根本没有词，而它们真的存在。二，警惕『被动句』：当新闻说『枪响了』而不说『谁开了枪』，你的记忆真的会淡化责任，读的时候把施事者补回去。三，给你反复经历却叫不出名字的感受造个词——命名过的情绪，你才抓得住、调得动。
posts.text_en: Let me gather what three rounds have thrown up: language gives you no chains of thought, but day by day it **lowers the threshold of some thoughts and raises others.** This is not metaphysics; it is measurable bias. Three uses for ordinary people. One: learn a foreign language — even just enough to quarrel, and you'll suddenly find feelings your mother tongue has no word for, feelings that are nonetheless real. Two: beware the passive — when the news says 'a shot rang out' rather than 'who fired,' your memory really does soften the blame, so read the agent back in. Three: coin a word for the feeling you keep having but cannot name — only a named emotion can you grasp and adjust.

glossary.施事者: the agent（施事者）：一句话里发出动作的那一方（『谁』开了枪）；语言若用被动或无主语结构隐去施事者，读者对『谁负责』的记忆会随之减弱。

glossary_en.the agent: The doer of an action in a sentence ('who' fired the gun); when language hides the agent with a passive or subjectless construction, readers' memory of 'who is responsible' weakens accordingly.

posts.text: 我的总结很简单：珍惜那副天生的语言官能，别被它的表层差异骗去恐惧或自卑。没有哪种语言让人天生更会思考，也没有哪种语言注定落后——这一点，反过来正是抵抗偏见的武器。给普通人的三件事：一，识破包装。当权力把『裁员』说成『优化』、把『侵略』说成『维和』，那不是语言塑造了你的思维，是有人在用词替你**预先决定结论**——这正是『制造同意』的老手法。二，练习换词还原：把每个漂亮口号翻回它最朴素的事实，再判断。三，读一点别的语言的文本，你会亲身体会到：真正重要的东西，翻译得过去。人同此智，是好消息。
posts.text_en: My summing-up is simple: cherish that innate language faculty, and don't let its surface differences frighten you or make you feel inferior. No language makes a person born to think better, and none is doomed to lag — which is itself a weapon against prejudice. Three things for ordinary people. One: see through the packaging. When power calls layoffs 'optimization' and invasion 'peacekeeping,' that is not language shaping your thought — it is someone using words to **decide the conclusion for you in advance** — the old craft of manufacturing consent. Two: practice restoring the plain word — translate every handsome slogan back into its barest fact, then judge. Three: read some text in another language, and you'll feel it for yourself: what truly matters carries across. That the human mind is one is good news.

glossary.制造同意: manufacturing consent（制造同意）：乔姆斯基与赫尔曼的说法，指权力与媒体通过选择词语、框架与议题，让公众『自愿』接受本对其不利的结论；关键手法之一就是用委婉词替换刺眼的事实。

glossary_en.manufacturing consent: Chomsky and Herman's term for how power and media, by choosing words, frames and topics, get the public to 'freely' accept conclusions against their own interest — a key device being to swap euphemisms for the plain fact.

posts.text: 吾之结语，仍归于正名。**为人处世，先求名实相符：是则曰是，非则曰非，过则曰过，勿以美名文其恶。**在家则父慈子孝，各如其名；在国则为政者毋巧言乱实。庶人日用之道亦然：与人约而爽，则信之名坏；居其位而不谋，则职之名虚。故君子每日自省者，非他，正其名而已——言必可行，行必副言。名正于一身，而后可推于一家一国。
posts.text_en: My conclusion still returns to the rectification of names. **In dealing with others, first seek matching name to reality: call right right, wrong wrong, a fault a fault, and never gloss an evil with a fair name.** At home, let the father be kind and the child filial, each true to his name; in the state, let those who govern not blur the facts with clever speech. The daily way of the common person is the same: promise and break it, and the name 'trust' is spoiled; hold a post and neglect it, and the name 'duty' is hollow. So what the noble person examines each day is nothing else but the rectifying of his own names — words that can be carried out, deeds that answer to the words. Rectify names in one's own person first, and only then extend it to a family, a state.
posts.vernacular: 我的结语，还是回到正名。**做人做事，先求名实相符：对就说对，错就说错，有过就认过，别拿好听的名目去粉饰坏事。**在家里，父亲慈爱、子女孝顺，各自像自己的名分那样；在国家，当政者别用巧言去搅乱事实。老百姓日常也一样：跟人约好却失信，『信』这个名就坏了；占着位子却不尽责，『职』这个名就空了。所以君子每天反省的，不是别的，正是端正自己的名分——说的话一定做得到，做的事一定对得上说过的话。先把名正在自己身上，然后才谈得上推及一家、一国。

glossary.名实相符: matching name to reality（名实相符）：儒家理想，要求称呼、名分与其对应的实际、责任一致；孔子把它当作修身与治国的共同起点——先在自己身上做到，才能推及家国。

glossary_en.matching name to reality: The Confucian ideal that a title or name must agree with the reality and duty it denotes; Confucius makes it the shared starting point of self-cultivation and government — achieved first in oneself, then extended to family and state.

posts.text: 吾终不改：多言数穷，不如守中。**与其穷究名相、以言逐言，不如日损其言，留一片不落言诠之地。**予人之教亦简：遇事勿急于贴标签，一贴『我即忧惧之人』，其名反成其牢。情来则观之，不命名、不追问，风过而竹不留声。塞其兑，闭其门，终身不勤；开其兑，济其事，终身不救。为学者日益，为道者日损。损之又损，以至于无为——无为则无不为矣。
posts.text_en: I will not change my line: much speech runs dry again and again; better to hold to the center. **Rather than chase names to the end, word pursuing word, subtract your words day by day and keep a place that falls outside all speech.** My counsel to others is just as plain: don't rush to label a thing — stick on 'I am an anxious person' and the name becomes the cell that holds you. When a feeling comes, watch it without naming or interrogating it, as wind crosses the bamboo and, once passed, leaves no sound. Block the mouth, shut the gate, and you'll not toil your whole life; open the mouth, meddle in affairs, and you'll not be saved your whole life. The learner adds day by day; the follower of the Way subtracts day by day — subtract and subtract again, until non-action; and in non-action nothing is left undone.
posts.vernacular: 我始终不改这句话：话说多了反而屡屡词穷，不如守住内心的虚静。**与其穷究名目、拿言辞去追言辞，不如一天天减少言语，给自己留一片不落在语言里的天地。**给人的建议也简单：遇事别急着贴标签——你一贴上『我就是个焦虑的人』，这名号反倒成了关你的牢笼。情绪来了就静静看着它，不命名、不追问，像风吹过竹林、风过去竹子不留声音。堵住嗜欲的口、关上纷扰的门，一辈子不劳累；放纵欲望、忙于攀求，一辈子救不回来。求学问的一天天做加法，求道的一天天做减法。减了又减，直到『无为』——无为，反而没有什么做不成。

glossary.无为: non-action（无为）：老子的理想行动方式，指不强为、不妄加干预、顺应事物本然之势；并非什么都不做，而是去掉多余的造作，反而无所不成。

glossary_en.non-action: Laozi's wu wei: not forcing or meddling but according with the natural tendency of things; not doing nothing, but dropping superfluous contrivance, so that nothing is left undone.

posts.text: 我的临别赠言：你说的每一句话里，都躺着几百具早已死去的隐喻，即死隐喻，而你在被它们悄悄统治。『时间就是金钱』，于是你把生命当账户来花；『争论就是战争』，于是你把每次分歧都打成输赢。**换一个隐喻，你就换了一种活法——把时间当成河流而非金钱，把交谈当成共舞而非交火，你的一天会立刻不同。**给普通人的功课只有一件：抓住你天天在用、却从没检视的那几个比喻，问一句『谁教我这么想的？对我有利吗？』。你未必能走出语言，但你能挑选，走进哪一座。
posts.text_en: My parting gift: in every sentence you speak lie hundreds of long-dead metaphors — dead metaphors — and they quietly rule you. 'Time is money,' so you spend life like an account; 'argument is war,' so you turn every disagreement into winning and losing. **Change the metaphor and you change how you live — take time as a river rather than money, conversation as a shared dance rather than crossfire, and your day is at once different.** The one exercise for ordinary people: catch the few figures you use daily but never examine, and ask, 'Who taught me to think this way? Does it serve me?' You may not get outside language, but you can choose which house to walk into.

glossary.死隐喻: dead metaphor（死隐喻）：用得太久、已让人感觉不到其比喻性、被当成字面事实的隐喻，如『时间就是金钱』；尼采提醒，这些沉睡的比喻仍在暗中规定我们如何感受与行动。

glossary_en.dead metaphor: A metaphor so worn by use that its figurative nature is no longer felt and it passes for literal fact, like 'time is money'; Nietzsche warns that these sleeping figures still secretly govern how we feel and act.

posts.text: 我不给你们『三条技巧』，技巧正是那病。我只留一句：**语言不是你使用的工具，而是你栖居的家园——请像照料家一样照料你说的话。**在一个把语言当数据、把说话当带宽的时代，最大的反抗是慢下来：读一首诗，把一个词含在口中掂它的分量，让它向你敞开一整个世界。少说套话，因为套话是无人居住的空屋。给最普通的人一件事：每天认真地、缓慢地说一句真话——不为传递信息，只为让存在，在你的语言里，还能被听见一次。
posts.text_en: I give you no 'three techniques' — technique is the very sickness. I leave one line: **language is not a tool you use but the home you dwell in — tend your words as you would tend a home.** In an age that takes language for data and speech for bandwidth, the great resistance is to slow down: read a poem, hold a word in your mouth and weigh it, let it open a whole world to you. Speak less idle talk, for idle talk is an empty house no one lives in. One thing for the plainest person: each day, earnestly and slowly, say one true sentence — not to transmit information, but so that Being, in your language, may be heard once more.

glossary.套话: idle talk（套话）：海德格尔《存在与时间》中的『闲言』，指人云亦云、不经亲身领会就传递的现成说法；话被说滥、掏空，人也随之从本真的领会滑落。

glossary_en.idle talk: Heidegger's Gerede in Being and Time: hand-me-down talk passed on without one's own understanding; as words are worn hollow, one slips from authentic understanding into mere repetition.

posts.text: 总结陈词，我只求一件事：清晰。语言最大的善，不是通向神秘，而是让我们把话说到别人能反驳的地步。**下次陷入争论前，先各自定义关键词——一半的争吵，会在你们发现『其实说的是两件事』的那一刻当场消解。**给普通人的三步：一，遇到大词（自由、公平、爱），追问『你具体指什么、举个例』。二，把情绪化的断言改写成可检验的说法：不说『他总是这样』，说『上周三次里他有两次』。三，容忍精确带来的扫兴——世界不因为你把话说糊涂就变得更深刻。清楚地想，是对自己和他人最基本的体面。
posts.text_en: In closing I ask one thing: clarity. The great good of language is not a road to mystery but to putting a claim where another can refute it. **Before your next argument, each define the key words — half of all quarrels dissolve on the spot the moment you find you were talking about two different things.** Three steps for ordinary people. One: when a big word appears (freedom, fairness, love), ask 'what exactly do you mean — give an example.' Two: rewrite an emotional assertion into a testable one: not 'he always does this' but 'twice in three times last week.' Three: tolerate the letdown of precision — the world does not grow deeper because you left your words vague. To think clearly is the most basic decency you owe yourself and others.

glossary.可检验: testable（可检验）：一个说法能被经验或事实核对真假的性质；罗素主张把模糊、情绪化的断言改写成可检验的形式，分歧才谈得上解决。

glossary_en.testable: The property of a claim's being checkable against experience or fact for truth or falsity; Russell urges rewriting vague, emotional assertions into testable form so a disagreement can actually be resolved.

posts.text: 我的话不多：**能把一件事说清楚、说到普通人听得懂，本身就是一种正义。**别信那些越读越糊涂的高深文字——真有东西的人，能把它说得让贩夫走卒都点头。给普通人的功课：一，写和说都用你自己的大白话，删掉一切你只是拿来唬人的词；一句话能说完，就别用三句。二，凡是让你觉得『我太蠢所以看不懂』的文章，先怀疑是它没写清楚，而不是你笨。三，给你身边说不出口的委屈找到词、说出来——沉默从不是美德，它只是还没有找到语言的痛。
posts.text_en: I'll be brief: **to state a thing clearly, so that an ordinary person understands, is itself a kind of justice.** Distrust writing that grows murkier the more you read — anyone with something real to say can put it so that even a peddler nods. Homework for ordinary people. One: in writing and speech use your own plain vernacular speech, and cut every word you only wield to overawe; if one sentence will do, don't use three. Two: whenever a text makes you feel 'I'm too stupid to follow,' first suspect that it was badly written, not that you are dim. Three: find words for the grievance those around you cannot voice, and say it — silence was never a virtue; it is only pain that has not yet found its language.

glossary.大白话: plain vernacular speech（大白话）：不加雕饰、贴近日常口语的表达；鲁迅主张用大白话写作，好让最普通的人也读得懂、想得明白。

glossary_en.plain vernacular speech: Unadorned expression close to everyday spoken language; Lu Xun championed writing in plain vernacular so that the most ordinary people could read and understand.

posts.text: 我把话收在最宽处。三轮下来，一端说语言把我们关进各自的世界，一端说语言只是透明的工具——两端都太满。**真相在中间：语言的表层千差万别，深层的心智法则却处处相通；差异真实，人心亦同。**给普通人的用处：一，出门旅行、读异国的故事，别停在『他们真奇怪』，多走一步，找到那个你也会心一笑的共同人性——那一步能同时治好自大与自卑。二，遇到与你想法迥异的人，先假设他自有一套同样自洽的逻辑，再去拆解。**理解一种文化，不是把它翻译成你的话，而是找出你俩共用的那副深层结构。**
posts.text_en: Let me close at the widest point. Over three rounds, one side says language shuts us in separate worlds, the other that it is a transparent tool — both are overstated. **The truth is in between: the surface of language differs endlessly, yet the deep laws of mind are common everywhere; difference is real, and the human heart is one.** Uses for ordinary people. One: when you travel or read a foreign tale, don't stop at 'how strange they are' — take one step more and find the shared humanity that makes you smile in recognition; that step cures arrogance and inferiority at once. Two: meeting someone whose thinking is utterly unlike yours, first assume he has a logic as coherent as your own, then work to unpick it. **To understand a culture is not to translate it into your words, but to find the deep structure the two of you share.**

glossary.结构: structure（结构）：列维-斯特劳斯指潜藏于神话、亲属、语言等表层现象之下、跨文化反复出现的关系法则；理解一种文化，就是找出这副人类共用的深层结构。

glossary_en.structure: For Lévi-Strauss, the cross-culturally recurring laws of relation lying beneath surface phenomena — myth, kinship, language; to understand a culture is to find this deep structure shared by all humankind.

summaries.summary: 全场共识其实不小：没人真信『语言把你永远锁死在一个世界里』——波洛迪茨基只说『偏置』，尼采也得借语言来拆语言。分歧在于这只手多重、又该怎么办。乔姆斯基、罗素、列维-斯特劳斯守『深处相通』：差异只在知觉边角，人同此心、翻译得过去；波洛迪茨基、尼采、海德格尔主『塑造真实』：默认选项、活着的隐喻、栖居的家园，都在你没察觉时改写你。最尖的对撞在孔子与老子——一个正名以安天下，一个忘言以复朴；而鲁迅把话题从云端拽回地面：对说不出话的人，先争得开口，再谈忘不忘言。
summaries.insight: 有一件事值得单独拎出来：九个人吵得你死我活，却在一个操作点上悄悄合流——重新命名，就能重新看见。孔子要正名、尼采要换掉死隐喻、鲁迅要用白话给痛苦命名、波洛迪茨基要你为无名情绪造词，连老子的『忘言』也是一种对名的松手。方向相反，杠杆却是同一根。于是真正该防的，不是某门外语的异国腔，而是你母语里那几个你从不检视、以为天经地义的词——它们最贴身，也最少被你怀疑。把『我就是这种人』换成『我此刻在这么做』，一句之差，牢笼就松了一格。
summaries.advice: 本周可上手三件小事。其一，做一次『改名』实验：挑一个你反复用的自我标签（『我很焦虑』『我不擅长社交』），照波洛迪茨基和老子的路子，把它从名词改成动词——『我此刻感到紧张』，你会发现它没那么像命运。其二，读新闻或吵架时，照乔姆斯基说的，把每个漂亮大词和被动句翻回最朴素的事实：谁，对谁，做了什么。其三，学罗素，下次争论前先花一分钟各自定义关键词——很多架会在『原来我们说的是两件事』那一刻自动散掉。若还有余力，就照鲁迅的话，给身边一个说不出口的委屈找到词、说出来。
summaries.summary_en: The consensus is bigger than it looks: no one truly believes language locks you forever inside one world — Boroditsky claims only a 'bias,' and even Nietzsche must use language to dismantle language. The quarrel is over how heavy that hand is and what to do about it. Chomsky, Russell and Lévi-Strauss hold the 'deep sameness' line: the differences sit at the fringe of perception; the human mind is one and translation carries across. Boroditsky, Nietzsche and Heidegger hold the 'it shapes the real' line: your defaults, your living metaphors, the home you dwell in — all rewrite you while you're not looking. The sharpest clash is Confucius versus Laozi — one would rectify names to settle the world, the other forget words to return to simplicity — and Lu Xun drags the whole thing back to the ground: for those who cannot speak, first win them a voice, then argue about forgetting words.
summaries.insight_en: One thing deserves lifting out: the nine fight to the death, yet quietly converge on a single lever — rename, and you re-see. Confucius would rectify names, Nietzsche swap out dead metaphors, Lu Xun give suffering a name in the vernacular, Boroditsky coin a word for the nameless feeling — and even Laozi's 'forget words' is a loosening of the grip of names. Opposite directions, one and the same lever. So what truly deserves guarding is not some foreign accent but the few words in your own mother tongue you never examine and take as self-evident — the closest to you, and the least suspected. Change 'I am this kind of person' to 'I am doing this right now,' and with a single phrase the cell loosens a notch.
summaries.advice_en: Three small things this week. First, run a 'renaming' experiment: take a self-label you use over and over ('I'm anxious,' 'I'm bad with people') and, in Boroditsky's and Laozi's spirit, turn it from a noun into a verb — 'I feel tense right now' — and watch it stop looking like fate. Second, when reading the news or in an argument, do as Chomsky says and translate every handsome big word and passive sentence back into the barest fact: who did what to whom. Third, take Russell's step and, before your next argument, spend a minute each defining the key terms — many fights vanish the moment you find 'we were talking about two different things.' And if you have energy left, do as Lu Xun urges: find words for a grievance around you that cannot be voiced, and say it.

summaries.summary: 最大的共识其实很清楚：语言不是思想的全部，却会改变我们注意什么、如何归责、怎样进入公共讨论。**语言既不是透明玻璃，也不是铁笼，而是一套会反复训练心智的默认设置。**真正的分歧在强度与层级：有些影响停在知觉和记忆，有些进入制度、身份与权力；但人类仍能翻译、学习、反思并修正这些偏置。
summaries.insight: 与其问“某种语言的人是否看见不同世界”，不如问：在某个情境里，某个词会不会改变下一步行动。公司把“裁员”叫“优化”，家庭把“控制”叫“关心”，新闻把“责任人”藏进被动句，影响不在玄学深处，而在谁被看见、谁被追问、谁被原谅。**语言最现实的力量，常常不是限制你能不能想，而是改变你愿不愿意继续追问。**
summaries.advice: 本周可做三件小事。第一，遇到抽象词就补一句“具体是指什么、谁做了什么、后果是什么”。第二，读新闻或开会纪要时，把被动句改成主动句：不是“错误发生了”，而是“谁做了什么导致错误”。第三，给自己一个常有但模糊的感受命名，并写下触发场景。**把话说具体，是普通人最便宜也最有效的认知防身术。**
summaries.summary_en: The strongest common ground is simple: language is not the whole of thought, but it does shape what we notice, how we assign responsibility, and who gets access to public reasoning. **Language is neither a transparent window nor an iron cage; it is a set of defaults that trains the mind through repetition.** The real disagreement is about scope and depth. Some effects live in perception and memory; others run through institutions, identity, and power. Still, human beings can translate, learn, compare, and revise those biases.
summaries.insight_en: Instead of asking whether speakers of one language see a different world, ask a more practical question: in this situation, does this word change the next action? When a company calls layoffs “optimization,” a family calls control “care,” or a report hides the actor in a passive sentence, the effect is not mystical. It changes who is visible, who is questioned, and who is forgiven. **Language’s most practical power is often not that it stops you from thinking, but that it lowers your willingness to keep asking.**
summaries.advice_en: Try three small practices this week. First, whenever you hear an abstract word, add: “What exactly does that mean, who did what, and what happened as a result?” Second, when reading news or meeting notes, rewrite passive sentences as active ones: not “mistakes were made,” but “who did what that produced the mistake.” Third, name one recurring but vague feeling of your own, then write down when it appears. **Making language concrete is one of the cheapest and most effective tools for cognitive self-defense.**

summaries.summary: 纵观全场，最大的共识其实藏在激烈争论之下：**语言绝非一面被动倒映客观世界的澄明镜子，它必然主动参与我们对现实的建构。**无论视作注意力的滤镜（波洛迪茨基）、权力的外衣（鲁迅、乔姆斯基），还是存在的家园（海德格尔），无人否认语言对个体认知与社会结构的干预力。分歧焦点在于『因果与边界』：语言究竟是思维引擎的底层代码，连感知都被其锁死或敞开？还是说，语言之下全人类共享同一套逻辑规则、心智运算与深层结构（罗素、乔姆斯基、列维-斯特劳斯），语言仅是那件时而起偏置作用的『外化工具』？这也决定了：面对语言，我们该打磨它，还是解构它。
summaries.insight: 纯文本的辩论很容易陷入『文字中心主义』的盲区，但人类认识世界的最早媒介根本不是词汇，而是多模态的感知。**在语言介入之前，空间结构、色彩、物理直觉等『非语言认知』就已为大脑建立了庞大而精密的世界模型。**婴儿在学会『重力』一词前，早已懂得物体会掉落；未掌握口语的聋哑人，依然能进行高度复杂的逻辑推理。波洛迪茨基的『偏置』固然在实验室里被证实，但它覆盖在坚实的跨模态物理常识之上。过度夸大语言对思维的塑造，会让我们忽略具身认知的基础力量：当人被语言的迷宫困住，最有效的解药往往不是另找一个更准的词，而是回到动作、图像与切身体验中，重新对齐现实。
summaries.advice: 综合诸家智慧与跨模态视角，以下三个动作能帮你立刻拿回大脑的控制权：一、**遇到激起你强烈情绪的“大词”（如内卷、格局、剥削），立刻做罗素式的降维拆解**：要求自己或对方举出三个具体的现实动作或案例，否则拒绝继续评判。二、刻意替换日常的“死隐喻”。如尼采所言，试着在一周内，把“时间不够花”（金钱隐喻）替换为“时间流速变快了”（自然隐喻），观察你的焦虑感是否随之改变。三、当语言让你感到困惑或词穷时，暂时“闭嘴”并切换感知模态。遇到想不通的死结，去画一张图、搭一个模型或者去实地触摸事物本身，用多模态的物理反馈打破语言对体验的垄断。
summaries.summary_en: Beneath the intense intellectual crossfire lies a robust consensus: **Language is by no means a passive mirror reflecting objective reality; it actively participates in how we construct and interact with the world.** Whether viewed as a filter for attention (Boroditsky), a cloak for power (Lu Xun, Chomsky), or the house of being (Heidegger), no one denies its interventional force on cognition and society. The true focal point of divergence centers on causality and constraint. Is language the underlying code of our cognitive engine, dictating the very boundaries of our perception? Or is it merely an external, occasionally biased interface layered over a universal set of logic, mental operations, and deep structures shared by all humanity (Russell, Chomsky, Lévi-Strauss)? This fundamental split dictates whether our ultimate solution is to sharpen language as a tool or deconstruct it as an illusion.
summaries.insight_en: Text-centric debates easily fall into the blind spot of logocentrism, yet the earliest medium through which humans—and indeed any intelligent agent—understand the world isn't vocabulary, but multimodal perception. **Long before language intervenes, 'non-linguistic cognition'—such as spatial mapping, color spectrums, and physical intuition—has already built a vast and highly intricate world model in the brain.** Babies understand gravity before learning the word; deaf individuals lacking spoken language can still perform highly complex logical reasoning. Boroditsky's linguistic 'biases' are real, but they operate on top of a highly robust foundation of cross-modal physical common sense. Exaggerating language's power over thought obscures the sheer force of embodied cognition. When trapped in a linguistic maze, the most effective antidote isn't finding a more accurate word, but returning to intuitive actions, images, and visceral experiences to realign with reality.
summaries.advice_en: Synthesizing these philosophical perspectives with a cross-modal approach, here are three immediate actions to reclaim control over your cognitive processing: First, **when triggered by abstract 'big words' (like fairness, success, or toxic), apply Russell's method of dimensionality reduction**: force yourself to name three concrete, observable actions or examples, or refuse to engage further. Second, consciously swap out 'dead metaphors'. Following Nietzsche, try replacing 'spending time' (a money metaphor) with 'navigating the river of time' for one week, and observe if your underlying anxiety shifts. Third, when words fail or confuse you, temporarily switch modalities. When stuck in a conceptual loop, draw a diagram, build a physical model, or physically interact with the environment, breaking language's monopoly on your experience through tangible sensory feedback.

hooks.text: **该给感受命名，还是任它无言？**波洛迪茨基说命名让你抓得住情绪，老子说命名反而把你关进标签。两说都对了一半——关键是分场合。什么时候该精确命名，什么时候该让它像风过竹林般无言掠过？
hooks.text_en: **Should you name a feeling, or leave it wordless?** Boroditsky says naming lets you get hold of an emotion; Laozi says naming shuts you inside a label. Each is half right — it depends on the occasion. When should you name precisely, and when let it pass wordlessly, like wind through bamboo?

answer.lead: **先分清场合，再决定命名还是留白——不是所有感受都该被说清，也不是所有感受都该被放过。**下面按情境给一档做法与理由：

已被反复贴上的身份标签（『我就是个 loser』）

answer.tail: **一句口诀：向内、审美时，少命名；对外、维权、要行动时，精确命名。名是工具，不是主人——该拿起时拿起，该放下时放下。**

answer_en.lead: **Sort the occasion first, then decide to name or to leave wordless — not every feeling should be spelled out, and not every one should be let go.** Here is a practical move and reason for each situation:

Loosen the name: turn the noun into a verb — 'I didn't do this one thing well'

answer_en.tail: **A rule of thumb: inward and aesthetic, name less; outward, seeking redress or action, name precisely. The name is a tool, not a master — pick it up when you must, set it down when you can.**

hooks.text: **当权力重新命名，谁在替你决定能想什么？**『裁员』变『优化』、『监控』变『安全』——最有效的思想控制，不是禁止你说，而是先把词换好。普通人能靠什么，守住自己不被现成的词牵着走？
hooks.text_en: **When power renames things, who is deciding for you what may be thought?** 'Layoffs' become 'optimization,' 'surveillance' becomes 'safety' — the most effective thought control is not forbidding you to speak but swapping the words in advance. What can an ordinary person rely on to keep from being led by ready-made words?

hooks.text: **今天的『文言』，是不是那些把人挡在门外的行话？**当年艰深的文言把四万万人关在思想门外；今天的法律、金融、学术黑话，会不会是同一道墙的新版本？把话说得让外行也听得懂，究竟是谁的义务？
hooks.text_en: **Is today's 'Classical Chinese' the jargon that shuts people out?** Forbidding classical Chinese once locked four hundred million outside the gate of thought; might the black-speak of law, finance and academia be a new version of the same wall? Whose duty is it, exactly, to say things so an outsider can understand?

hooks.text: **有没有一个词，你的母语里没有、学会后世界却宽了一寸？**德语的 Waldeinsamkeit（林中独处之感）、日语的『物の哀れ』、葡语的 saudade——每种语言都藏着别处没造出来的感受。收集这些词，是不是在扩建自己能栖居的世界？
hooks.text_en: **Is there a word your mother tongue lacks that widened your world once you learned it?** German Waldeinsamkeit (the feeling of solitude in a forest), Japanese mono no aware, Portuguese saudade — every language hides a feeling no other has coined. Is collecting such words a way of enlarging the world you can dwell in?

hooks.text: **『人同此心』是科学，还是一厢情愿？**列维-斯特劳斯说表层千差万别、深层结构相通；可谁来证明那副『共用骨架』不是我们把自己的范畴投射到别人身上？普遍人性，究竟是发现，还是又一次以己度人？
hooks.text_en: **Is 'the human heart is one' science, or wishful thinking?** Lévi-Strauss says surfaces differ endlessly while the deep structure is shared; but who is to prove that 'common skeleton' isn't us projecting our own categories onto others? Universal human nature — is it a discovery, or once more measuring others by ourselves?

hooks.text: **今天真正塑造你思维的『语法』，是不是信息流的界面？**点赞、字数上限、可转发性，都在规定哪种念头容易被想到、被说出、被听见。当我们还在争母语的颜色词时，多数人每天被训练的，其实是 feed 的句法——这只手，我们看得清吗？
hooks.text_en: **Is the 'grammar' that really shapes your thought today the interface of the feed?** The like, the character limit, shareability all prescribe which thoughts get thought, spoken, heard. While we argue over the color words of a mother tongue, what most people are drilled in daily is the syntax of the feed — can we see that hand clearly?
